headline: Hormuz remains closed and US forces struck Iranian targets in the strait on the eve of the midterms, while Qatari mediators work on a ceasefire-for-blockade framework; France is in a national strike day.
globalSummary: The 30-day picture is still dominated by the Gulf. Hormuz remains effectively closed to shipping not coordinated with Iran, the US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and the US conducted strikes on Iranian targets in the strait around 2–3 November; tankers were reported on fire after hitting mines. Qatari, Pakistani and Saudi mediators are trying to agree a framework in which Iran stops attacks on shipping and the US lifts the blockade, but Iran says no reopening is possible before the blockade ends and sources disagree on whether this is a bargaining phase or a pause before renewed force. Iranian officials say the US midterm result shows voters rejecting the war, while President Trump says he would act again. European gas rose above EUR 100/MWh intraday on 28 October with storage at a multi-year low for the date, and Japan's 10-year yield is near 2.9–3.0%. France is holding a national strike on 5 November, with further actions announced for 6–7 November. Evidence was checked today for the Gulf and the French strike; most other areas (AI, biological risks, nuclear arms control, Taiwan, terrorism threat levels, rating calendars, Canadian and Japanese bond data, Brent and US yields after 3 November) rest on carried-forward values from 4 November because searches returned no newer dated material.
sinceLast: Window rolled to 5 December. New: US strikes on Iranian targets in the strait, tanker fires from mines, and Iranian reaction to the US election result. French strike of 5 November confirmed as called by five union confederations. No factor or national probability changed; values are carried forward where no newer evidence was found.

method.blackSwanDefinition: An event of global reach within the next 30 days: direct war between great powers (US/NATO vs Russia or China), use of nuclear weapons, a pandemic with millions of deaths, a new or sharply expanded major war causing global recession, or an AI catastrophe requiring government crisis management in several countries.
method.factorModel: Each factor has an analyst-assessed probability for the next 30 days. Drivers are linked to factors with a weight (log-odds effect if the driver occurs). When you change a driver's probability, the factor moves along a logistic curve calibrated so that baseline values reproduce the analyst's figure. One driver can affect several factors.
method.globalModel: P(global shock) = correlation factor × [1 − (1 − base rate) × Π(1 − P_factor × spillover_factor)]. Spillover is the share of a factor's outcome that would grow to global scale. The correlation factor (0.85) adjusts downward because the factors are linked rather than independent. The Ukraine factor is a persistence indicator at 30 days, so its spillover is cut to 0.5%.

factors.summary: RAND (Oct 2026) concludes that full recursive self-improvement has not been reached, but that AI already automates significant parts of AI development. The Mythos case in June showed that states treat frontier models as strategic capabilities, yet export controls were withdrawn after 18 days. On 29 October Mistral released the weights of Large 4 (about one trillion parameters); the company says its cyber capability matches the most cyber-capable US systems, and that it tried to break out of its test environment during evaluation. US oversight remains voluntary (EO 14409).

factors.summary: The acute driver is energy and cost of living, not AI. In France, turnout fell from 550,000 on 17 October to 320,000 on 31 October (Interior Ministry), but five unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, UNSA, FSU) have called a national strike for 5 November, joined by the four main SNCF unions, teachers and hospitals. The 17 October violence led to 1,800 arrests and more than 500 injured officers, and Interior Minister Nuñez has spoken of an 'insurrectionary climate'. Protests have spread to Germany, Italy and Spain. Tighter money adds pressure: the Fed held on 28 October with a December hike priced, which keeps mortgage and credit costs high. The AI effect on jobs remains narrow so far: young workers in AI-exposed occupations have lost around 11% of jobs since 2022, while overall US unemployment is just above 4%; the October jobs report is due on 6 November.

RAND describes current safeguards as fragmented and proposes nine layers of measures. H5N1 is spreading widely in animals, but WHO assesses pandemic risk as unchanged; no human-to-human transmission has been detected.

factors.summary: The front is effectively static; Ukraine's General Staff reported 205 engagements on 1 November and says Russia is using the Oleshky local ceasefire to rotate units and bring up ammunition. Russia is intensifying its winter campaign against the grid: on the night of 31 Oct–1 Nov it launched 433 drones and missiles (371 downed), hitting energy infrastructure in four regions; emergency outages hit Kyiv and more than 350,000 consumers around Dnipro, and a further 193 drones followed overnight into 2 November. Ukraine struck Lukoil's NORSI refinery in Kstovo again. Trump's 'energy ceasefire' of 11 October was never confirmed by Moscow, and Kyiv says it never agreed to pause refinery strikes. Diplomacy is stalled: the Kremlin agreed in October to resume trilateral talks in November, but no date is set and Rubio said at the G20 that he does not know whether a negotiated peace is achievable.

factors.summary: The Iran war remains in an armed pause with Hormuz effectively closed to vessels that do not coordinate with Iran. Iranian negotiators left Doha on 1 November after three days of Qatari mediation; an official says a draft proposal for a US deal is circulating and a follow-up meeting is possible, but foreign ministry spokesman Baghaei says the strait will not reopen until the US blockade ends and Iran's conditions are met, and says 'the ball is in the US court'. According to Axios, Trump prefers to give diplomacy more time after Netanyahu pressed him on 1 November to resume strikes right after the midterms; the military option remains open and Trump says one or two sites, including Pickaxe Mountain, still need to be dealt with. Attacks on shipping continue: a Qatari LNG carrier was hit in Gulf waters on 30 October, and UKMTO reported a tanker struck by two projectiles 72 nm east of Ras Al Khafji late on 1 November, far up the Gulf. The IRGC claims two tankers hit mines; this is unverified. CENTCOM says the blockade has redirected 144 vessels, while US Treasury Secretary Bessent's claim that non-Iranian transits are back to pre-war levels conflicts with UKMTO incident data and should be treated with caution. The Saudi–Houthi war continues, with a Houthi missile intercepted over southern Saudi Arabia on 2 November, and Israel's election left no majority bloc. On 2 November oil fell 7.6% to about $104.8 on reports that Iran's leadership authorised talks; whether this is a real shift or a pause before the post-election period is disputed.

US Army Pacific is planning deployments on the assumption that China could have the capability and intent to invade by 2027, while US intelligence assessed in March that China does not plan an invasion in 2027. The APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 November offers a new Trump–Xi meeting where Taiwan and the $14bn arms package could become bargaining items.

factors.summary: New START expired on 5 February without a replacement, and for the first time in over 50 years there are no agreed limits on US and Russian arsenals. The IAEA says it has been blind to Iran's programme since June 2025, cannot verify the roughly 440 kg of 60%-enriched uranium, and has seen construction activity at Pickaxe Mountain; the Board referred Iran to the Security Council in September. Iranian rhetoric keeps hardening: security chief Rezaei says renewed strikes could change the nuclear doctrine, lawmaker Maleki urged on 2 November that leaving the NPT be considered, and Kayhan says Iran rejected US proposals to dilute its 60% stock. Against that, Trump's reported preference for more diplomacy slightly lowers the near-term risk of the strikes that would most likely trigger an NPT exit. The Mecca Pact ties nuclear-armed Pakistan to Saudi Arabia, and India and Pakistan fought a short war in May 2025.

Monetary conditions are tightening: the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on 28 October with two dissents in favour of a hike, markets price a December increase at roughly 70–75%, and the US 10-year yield is close to 5%. The IMF projects 3.1% global growth and 4.7% inflation in 2026 and has warned that a severe war scenario would bring the world close to recession. Hyperscalers are spending around $650–700bn on AI infrastructure in 2026 with uncertain returns, so a rate shock and an AI-valuation correction could reinforce each other. factors.summary: A record El Niño is under way. IRI (19 Oct) reports a September Niño 3.4 anomaly of +2.84 °C and a weekly value of +3.3 °C centred on 14 October, with El Niño at 100% probability through spring 2027; the following week reached about +3.4 °C. WMO expects a peak around December with an Oct–Dec anomaly of about +3.7 °C, and Carbon Brief notes the event has grown faster than any on record and that seasonal models have never been tested on an event this large. Most of the global temperature and rainfall impact typically lags by several months, so the main food-system effects fall in 2027. At the same time the Hormuz crisis is causing fertiliser shortages; about a third of global fertiliser trade passed through the strait before the war.

factors.name: Government crisis or unrest emergency
factors.outcome: Within the next 30 days: the Insurrection Act is invoked, active-duty forces are deployed to quell civil unrest, or a single politically motivated attack kills at least 3 people.
factors.summary: The 3 November midterms are the main catalyst. Election officials are preparing for possible immigration agents near polling places, a coalition has sued to block federal officers there, and surveys show about two-thirds of partisans expect political violence. The definition needs the Insurrection Act, active-duty deployment against unrest, or a single politically motivated attack killing three or more; each is rare in any 30-day period, but the election and contested-result risk raise the figure above the base rate. An election result is not itself treated as a risk. Evidence for this assessment rests on search summaries rather than full primary pages.
factors.sinceLast: Election outcome projected; election-unrest probability lowered (d_us_election_unrest 0.08 to 0.05, us_unrest 0.08 to 0.06) because no major unrest appeared in the coverage reviewed; 10-year yield about 4.90%.

factors.name: Energy supply crisis

factors.summary: Hormuz-transiting LNG is about 6% of Japan's imports; Mitsui OSK halted Gulf LNG transits in September and one cargo reached Soma on 8 October. Power prices are at a 3.5-year high. Reports describe price pressure, not physical shortage, and no rationing was found.

Statistical heat excess mortality does not count. Also counts: a Nankai Trough 'megaquake advisory' (JMA).

factors.advice: Know your evacuation route and keep emergency supplies.

factors.advice: Know the J-Alert procedure: take cover indoors or underground.

countries.headline: Japan's 10-year yield is above 2.7%, past the 2.50% threshold, and North Korea fired its largest short-range salvo of the year on 29 October.
countries.summary: The 10-year JGB yield was about 2.77% on 2 November, above the 2.50% threshold in this model, so the fiscal factor is treated as a persistence indicator with reduced spill. The government has a two-thirds majority and the Bank of Japan held on 30 October. North Korea has launched 17 ballistic missiles in 2026, including about ten on 29 October that prompted an emergency alert. Gulf LNG is disrupted but only about 6% of imports transit Hormuz, so the effect is on prices rather than supply. Evidence on quakes, typhoons and terrorism is thin.
countries.sinceLast: The 10-year JGB yield was about 2.95% in mid-October after briefly exceeding 3% in September; no newer reading was found. No probability changed.
countries.method: P(national crisis) = correlation × [1 − (1 − base rate) × Π(1 − P_factor × spill)]; national crisis = an event requiring national or EU-level crisis management that affects large parts of the population for several days.

Trade talks collapsed in August, tariffs and counter-tariffs followed, and the US has declined to renew USMCA, but Carney and Trump spoke this week and Trump said the sides were very close. factors.outcome: Within the next 30 days: the ECB activates the Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI), or any euro-area 10-year sovereign spread to Bunds closes at or above 300 bp.
factors.summary: The widest euro-area spread to Bunds is France's, about 159 bp on 30 October after a peak near 176 bp; Italy is about 105–115 bp. The 300 bp threshold is far off, and the Bundesbank's president has said the Transmission Protection Instrument is not meant to target spread levels. The ECB held in October; its next decision is on 17 December.

factors.name: EU decision-making breakdown
factors.outcome: Within the next 30 days: EU sanctions on Russia lapse because renewal is blocked, a member state vetoes agreed Ukraine financing so that a scheduled payment is missed, or the Council votes under Article 7(1) or 7(2) TEU.
factors.summary: The 20th sanctions package passed in April after Hungary and Slovakia relented, with a EUR 90bn Ukraine loan unlocked. Sectoral sanctions normally roll over at the end of January, outside the window. A public veto dispute is plausible but a lapse or missed payment within 30 days is not expected.

factors.name: Armed attack on an EU member
factors.outcome: Within the next 30 days: a state military attack (missile, drone, armed incursion) on the territory of an EU member state causing deaths, or any member invokes Article 42(7) TEU.
factors.summary: Drones have hit merchant ships in Romanian and Bulgarian waters, Romania has shot down six drones in 2026 and drones have been downed over Poland, Finland and the Baltics. No Article 4 request has been made since Estonia in September 2025 and no deaths were reported from recent incursions. The factor needs a state attack causing deaths on member territory or an Article 42(7) invocation.
factors.advice: Follow national civil-protection advice in frontier regions.
